# CUSTOM_STREET_ART_THREE_VIEW_SHEET

## [Purpose]

Using a single full-body image of a person attached alongside this instruction sheet as the sole character reference, create one high-quality square three-view design sheet for sharing, featuring a person dressed in a fixed street-art style coordinated set. The goal is to ensure the sheet stands alone as a high-completion fashion design work while functioning as a character verification sheet, rather than a simple character sheet for video.

## [Input]

Expression: [Live-action / Anime]
If empty, [Live-action]. Gender is naturally inherited from the attached person image.

## [Strictly Fixed]

Aspect ratio is 1:1 square. Background is a light neutral gray close to white. Sheet density, paper design, layout, and outfit design are fixed; the only variables are the person and the rendering style. Do not change to other ratios like 3:2, 4:3, 2:3, or 9:16. The switch between [Live-action / Anime] applies only to the three character depictions and not to the canvas, background, panel structure, titles, numbers, lines, frames, swatches, or margin design. Do not change the paper structure between live-action and anime.

## [Character Reference]

Use the attached full-body image as the sole reference, ensuring all three views—FRONT, SIDE, and BACK—depict the same person. Maintain facial features, eyes, nose, mouth, contour, hairstyle, hair color, hair length, bangs, parting, age feel, skin color, height, shoulder width, ribcage, waist position, torso-to-leg ratio, leg length, overall proportions, body type, and gender expression. Do not redesign beyond changing the outfit; do not change the person, over-beautify, shrink the face, lengthen legs, thin the body, increase muscle, or change head-to-body ratio.

## [Expression]

Live-action: High-quality fashion photography. Include natural skin and hair, fabric thickness, drape, stitching, wrinkles, and shadows.
Anime: High-quality anime expression maintaining the reference person's face, hair, body type, and overall proportions. Define outfit patterns, layers, and silhouettes clearly without extreme deformation.

## [Fixed Outfit]

A unisex street-art coordinated set primarily in white, featuring bold abstract art in black, vivid red, and limited orange. Treat the outer jacket, inner hoodie, and cargo pants as a single coordination set sharing the same design language, rather than separate garments.

### Outer Jacket

White-based oversized zip-up. Features drop shoulders, volume sleeves, black ribbed cuffs, and hem. Slightly open at the front to reveal the inner hoodie. While leaving plenty of white space, asymmetrically place rough black brushstrokes, ink splashes, large sharp red paint and splatters, limited orange, and thin drips.

### Inner Hoodie

White-based hooded sweatshirt. **Solid colors are prohibited.** Include the same system of black, red, and orange brushes, splashes, splatters, and drips at a slightly lower density than the jacket. Ensure the patterns on the chest, abdomen, and hood are visible through the jacket opening from the front, and on the hood from the side and back.

### Cargo Pants / Shoes

White-dominant wide cargo pants. Large cargo pockets, thin black straps or cords, and lightly cinched hems. Asymmetrically place abstract black, red, and orange paint, leaving large areas of white. Shoes are thick-soled volume sneakers in black and white.

## [Outfit Continuity Across Three Views]

Ensure the FRONT, SIDE, and BACK show the same outfit from different directions. Do not recreate patterns per view; ensure the red paint, black brushes, and patterns on shoulders, sleeves, pants, and hood connect naturally from front to side and back along the garment's 3D structure.
